messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated paging and p95 tail latency observed for kv-shard-svc (tensor-parallel). Paging events rising across multiple GPU nodes, autoscaling and continuous-batcher warnings firing. thread=2145701234

alex (oncall): acknow. grabbing dashboards and recent deploys. linking logs.

maria (kv-runtime): seeing repeated NCCL TIMEOUT in tp-shard logs starting ~2026-03-15T16:02:10Z. also kvcache reports shard_byte_count mismatch between ranks. sample log: 
```
[2026-03-15T16:02:12Z] NCCL WARN AllGather timeout rank 2 -> rank 3
[2026-03-15T16:02:12Z] kvcache: shard_bytes expected=524288 actual=655360
[2026-03-15T16:02:13Z] continuous_batcher: queue_length jumped to 4x baseline
```

alex (oncall): any recent config flips for batching or sharding?

maria (kv-runtime): we pushed a batching tuning 2.5h ago to reduce latency under small requests (KV_BATCH_AGGRESSIVENESS went from 0.5 -> 0.8 and continuous batching enabled for more routes). Hypothesis: increased aggressive batching + rounding bug in TP shard stride produced uneven partition sizes, causing NCCL imbalance and stalls, which in turn allowed in-memory queues to grow and trigger paging.

jordan (sre): customer impact? errors or timeouts surfaced?

ops-bot: Impact summary: approx 10-14% of /v1/generate requests in us-west1 and eu-west1 hit >2s tail latency. No 5xxs observed. Two enterprise customers opened support tickets citing sluggish responses. Overall throughput not fully degraded but tail is bad.

alex (oncall): initial mitigation plan: 1) flip continuous batching off for kv-shard-svc 2) roll back aggressive batch tunables to previous values 3) perform staggered tp-shard daemon restarts to reestablish NCCL rings 4) enable emergency shard stride fallback to enforce even partitioning.

tina (eng-runtime): I have a hotfix for shard stride rounding guard and a quick env toggle. Proposing envs: KV_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false, KV_BATCH_AGGRESSIVENESS=0.55, KV_SHARD_STRIDE_FALLBACK=1. Patch ready, canary to one pod first.

maria (kv-runtime): applying canary envs now. commands: 
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/kv-shard-svc KV_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false KV_BATCH_AGGRESSIVENESS=0.55 KV_SHARD_STRIDE_FALLBACK=1
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/kv-shard-svc --grace-period=30
```

alex (oncall): will restart tp-shard daemons rank-by-rank to avoid full ring outage. draining rank 0 -> restart -> wait stable -> continue.

eng-alert-bot: Canary pod shows 72% reduction in paging events, p95 down from 3.6s to 1.2s on that pod. NCCL WARNs absent from canary logs.

jordan (sre): good. start rolling to remainder with 60s stagger. notify CS to message impacted customers with ETA ~30m.

customer-success: informed customers in impacted list, gave preliminary update and ETA. will send confirmation when metrics stable.

maria (kv-runtime): rolling restarts underway. monitoring cluster memory, page-in/out, NCCL logs. so far consistent improvement as each pod flips.

ops-bot: Note: rolling back batch aggressiveness will increase token-cost slightly on small inference workloads; autoscaler may spin up extra pods. fallback routing to smaller model variant prepared if we see capacity cliffs.

tina (eng-runtime): queued merge for shard rounding guard into main, but deferring deploy until after incident. follow-ups: add unit tests for even-shard allocation, add a canary gate for batching config changes, add automated circuit-breaker to disable continuous batching if page rate > 4x baseline.

alex (oncall): preparing handoff notes: root cause hypothesis = interaction between aggressive continuous batching config and a tensor-parallel shard sizing rounding bug that produced uneven shard byte allocations -> NCCL imbalance/timeouts -> inflight batch queue growth -> OS-level paging and p95 tail spikes. Mitigations applied: batching toggled off, batch aggressiveness rolled back, shard-fallback enabled, tp-shard daemons restarted staggered.

oncall-handoff-bot: Handoff planned: alex -> maria at 2145709800. include pager and #oncall.

maria (kv-runtime): taking overnight watch. will own postmortem and coordinate runtime + SRE. will attach logs, timeline, and suggested preventative tests. monitoring for 3h window before marking incident resolved.

alex (oncall): filing incident ticket and linking this thread. closing active paging alerts; keep sensitivity up for 2 hours. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

-- end of thread --
